SURVEYING
● It is a branch of civil engineering that enables engineers to determine the
relative position of points on the surface of the earth.
● Before the start of most of the civil engineering work, surveying of the land is
carried out.
● A plan consisting of all the existing features on the ground and their relative
positions.
Types of Surveying
1. Plane Surveying – 250 Sq.km
2. Geodetic Surveying – Curvature of Earth (> 250 Sq.km)

● Topographical Survey: To Locate the natural and artificial
features on the surface of the earth.
● Cadastral Surveys: To determine boundaries of houses and
large buildings.
● City Surveys: To lay out the boundaries of plots for the
location of water supply and sewer lines.
● Mine Surveys: The underground mineral wealth, such as iron
ores, coal, gold, etc. are explored.

STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING
Structural Engineering is the process of designing a structure to
safely withstand all the forces expected on the structure in the most
cost-effective manner.
The process involves the following steps
● Understanding the need for the structure.
● Load calculation.
● Structural framing.
● Analysis.
● Fixing elements or member sizes with appropriate material.
● Prepare structural drawings.

TRANSPORTATION ENGINEERING
DEFINITION:
Branch of Civil Engineering that deals with the construction of
infrastructure to facilitate the transportation of Human beings, materials
and other goods.
MODES OF TRANSPORTATION:
● Land: The most commonly and extensively used mode of
transportation. The two biggest modes of land transport are Roadways
and Railways.
● Air: The second most popular mode of transportation is airways.
● Water: The most preferred mode of transportation of goods and
commodities internationally is through waterways.

ROADWAYS
● Handle the planning, designing, Construction, Operation of roads and other
vehicular facilities.
● Highway and road alignment.
● Estimate the transportation needs of public.
● Analyze locations of high traffic volumes and high collisions to ensure safety
and capacity.
● Use Civil engineering principles to improve transportation system.
● Utilize the three design parameters i.e., the driver, Vehicle and the roads
judicially while designing.

-- 37 of 51 --

RAILWAYS
● Handles the design, construction and operation of railroads.
● Design, construction and operation of mass transit systems like metro and
monorails.
● To include horizontal and vertical alignment of rails, surveying and leveling.
● Decide the station location, design and cost estimation.

-- 38 of 51 --

AIPORT AND HARBOUR
● To Fix the location of airport based on requirement and topography.
● To account for the impact and demands of aircraft.
● Design and construction of air traffic control.
● Analysis of predominant wind directions for orientation and design of runway.
● To design and construction of harbors and ports.
● Handle the operation of ports.

ROLES OF A TRANSPORTATION ENGINEER
● Handle planning, designing, construction and operation of roads and
highways.
● Estimate the public's transportation needs and the road network's capacity to
plan safe traffic management systems.
● Analyse locations of high traffic volume and resolve conflict to ensure safety.
● Planning, designing and construction of railway network.
● Planning, designing, constructing and operating mass transit systems like
monorails and metro rails.
● Decide and design station location for minimum running cost and maximum
utilization.
● Decide the location of the airport based on requirements and topography.
● Analyse predominant wind directions for orientation and design of the runway.
● Planning and design of air traffic control.
● Handle planning, designing and construction of ports and harbours.

ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING
● Environmental engineering can be described as a branch of applied
science and technology that addresses the issue of energy
conservation, production asset and control of waste from human and
animal activities.
● It also includes studies on the environmental impact of proposed
construction projects.
SUB BRANCHES:
● Water supply and treatment.
● Waste water treatment.
● Air pollution control.
● Solid and hazardous waste management.
● Environmental Impact Assessment.

-- 41 of 51 --

Excellence and Service
CHRIST

WATER SUPPLY AND WASTE WATER TREATMENT
WATER TREATMENT PLANT
• In environmental engineering water is
categorised into potable water and waste water.
WATER SUPPLY
• The role of an environmental engineer is to store,
treat and convey potable water for various uses
like drinking, domestic use and irrigation.
• Water is treated to achieve the water quality for
the required use.
• Water distribution systems are suitably designed
to provide adequate water pressure.
WASTE WATER TREATMENT
• Consists of primary classifier system to remove
solid and floating materials.
• A secondary treatment system consisting of an
aeration basin followed by sedimentation or an
activated sludge system.
• A tertiary biological nitrogen removal system.
• Final Disinfection process.

SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT
● It is the collection, transport,
processing, disposal and
monitoring of solid waste.
● Waste may be produced due to
direct or indirect human activity.
● Waste management is a process
which focuses on delaying the rate
of consumption of natural
resources.
● Management of waste treats all
materials as a single class
irrespective of solid, liquid or radio
active substances.

WATER RESOURCES ENGINEERING
• It is a branch of civil engineering with the collection, storage,
transportation and management of water as a natural
resource.
• It relates to predicting and managing the quantity of water
above the ground and underground.
• Water resource engineers analyze and model areas of the
earth to predict the amount of water collected and
discharged.
It consists of several sub-branches:
• Hydrology.
• Groundwater geology.
• Hydraulic engineering.

● Designing: Architectural, Structural, Electrical, HAVC, Plumbing
